6. NEW FINDING — ORPHAN-REMOVAL BYPASS GAP FOR FORCE-INJECTED STUBS: Rule 33 mandates that force-injected stubs bypass 'the compiler's priority-score selection gate AND the absorber's merge/trim stages.' However, 'absorbed' and 'trimmed_spurs' are the absorber's merge/trim operations; 'removed_orphans' is a SEPARATE disposal stage not explicitly named in Rule 33's bypass. This round proves the orphan-removal stage is active (removed_orphans=2). A force-injected Kelvin stub targeting a currently-sparse net may appear topologically orphaned to the orphan-removal heuristic (only stub for that net, little existing copper on it), causing it to be silently discarded before FR sees it — exactly the failure mode that makes force-injection ineffective. This gap is not covered by any existing rule: Rule 33 covers compiler gate + absorber; Rules 19/extended Rule 19 cover orphan audit after-the-fact but do not pre-emptively protect force-injected stubs from orphan removal.

Scorer penalty: null — existing weights already heavily penalize all failing metrics (kelvin_unrouted 1000, gate_fail 1000, unconnected 450, drc 75). Adding further weight on an already-penalized metric would not improve convergence and risks distorting the objective for rounds where those metrics improve partially.
manager_rule: When a 'compiler_kelvin_omission' event fires for round R (per Rule 33) AND the total-stub-absorption condition also fires in the same round (absorbed + trimmed_spurs + removed_orphans >= n_stubs), the force-injected Kelvin stubs mandated by Rule 33 MUST explicitly bypass the orphan-removal stage in addition to the compiler priority-score gate and absorber merge/trim stages already required by Rule 33. Rationale: the total-stub-absorption condition confirms the orphan-removal stage is actively discarding stubs this round (removed_orphans > 0); a force-injected Kelvin stub targeting a currently-unrouted net may appear topologically orphaned to the heuristic (it is the only stub for a sparse net), causing silent disposal before FR sees it — defeating the force-injection entirely. Implementation: tag each force-injected stub with a 'mandatory_kelvin_bypass' flag at injection time; the orphan-removal stage MUST unconditionally forward any stub carrying this flag without applying topology or coverage heuristics. Log 'force_injected_stub_orphan_bypass_active' with fields: (a) round number, (b) the Kelvin cable indices receiving force-injected stubs, (c) the net names of all force-injected stubs with bypass flag active. This rule is additive to Rule 33 and does not replace or defer any halt or action Rule 33, Rule 19, Rule 21, Rule 27, or Rule 29 would independently impose on the same round.
